uncited: **Feature Detection & Projection:** Perform ray casting through the volume.
*   *GPU Search Circle:* For each pixel outside the feature, search within a circle of maximal radius $l_b$ for the closest neighbor pixel that is part of the projected feature.
**Volume Rendering:** Cast rays with the modified directions through the volume.
Let $P$ be the pixel entry point on the image plane.
Let $F$ be the focal point in world space.
Let $d$ be the distance from $P$ to the boundary of the feature-projected area.
*(Note: The sources state "new direction is pointing to F".
In a standard pinhole camera, rays originate from the eye.
The "direction" here refers to the vector from the image plane point towards the focal point, effectively bending the ray path.)*
*   *Mitigation:* Use volume texture mip-mapping to adaptively choose the appropriate resolution of the volume data for rendering.
*   **Time Complexity:** The pre-computation of the distance field is $O(W \cdot H \cdot l_b^2)$ if using a naive search circle, where $W, H$ are image dimensions and $l_b$ is the transition width.
The main rendering pass is $O(N)$ where $N$ is the number of voxels sampled along rays.
